Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaCorp Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing questions will be given at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaCorp's Q3 results. With me on the call are Jordan Hayes, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Larson, Chief Marketing Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Hayes.

Jordan Hayes:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. NovaCorp delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

To provide some context before we get into the numbers, let me highlight our key strategic priorities and the progress we made this quarter. Our guiding principle is to achieve consistent growth that outperforms the broader CPG sector, which saw just 2.1% constant-currency expansion in North America according to IRI data. We're advancing across four core pillars: innovation-led portfolio optimization, digital and omnichannel acceleration, sustainability and ESG leadership, and operational resilience in the face of macroeconomic challenges.

On innovation-led portfolio optimization, we've been aggressively premiumizing, shedding underperforming legacy items like certain pantry basics that eroded margins, and ramping up investment in high-potential areas such as health-oriented snacks and functional drinks. This quarter, we introduced 12 fresh SKUs in our NovaSnax protein bars and HydroBoost electrolyte beverages, riding trends similar to those boosting Clif Bar and Prime Hydration. These drove 9% of our revenue increase, with premium items—now comprising 42% of the snack lineup—expanding 14% versus 7% for the full segment. We gained 2,500 ACV points in North America for NovaSnax, reaching 68% overall ACV, while velocity rose 11% in club stores like Costco and Sam's Club. Meanwhile, we divested a regional baking brand for $125 million, freeing up funds for R&D spend that's up 18% year-over-year to 2.8% of sales. Early wins include our plant-based almond-protein clusters, which grabbed 3.2 share points in the $4.2 billion clean-label snack space, surpassing private label advances.

Shifting to digital and omnichannel acceleration, e-commerce now accounts for 22% of North American sales, up from 14% last year, capitalizing on lasting pandemic shifts. Beyond Amazon, our DTC site NovaCorp Direct surged 45% to a $180 million run-rate, with 65% repeat rates fueled by AI recommendations for personalized subscriptions. Key partnerships include exclusive Instacart ties with Whole Foods 365 for 28% natural channel growth and Shopify-powered Target Plus pop-ups lifting Gen Z buys by 15%. Internationally, HydroBoost velocity on Shopee and Lazada in APAC jumped 62%, securing a 200 basis point share increase to 12.4% NMV in Southeast Asia's RTD beverages per Kantar. We're on track for digital to hit 25% of total revenue by fiscal 2025, exceeding plans.

In sustainability and ESG leadership, we're delivering where consumers expect action—Nielsen notes 78% of millennials favor eco-packaging. We've reached 95% recyclable or compostable packaging across core lines ahead of schedule, including mono-material PET for HydroBoost that cuts virgin plastic 30%. Scope 1 and 2 emissions dropped 22% year-over-year via regenerative ag deals with suppliers like Cargill for oats. This drives value: our Core Green range grew 19%, at a 25% premium, landing us top-5 in the 2024 Dow Jones Sustainability Index for CPG. In EMEA, amid tightening EU Packaging Directive rules, we've added 150 basis points in sustainable personal care share through circular economy pilots akin to Unilever collaborations.

Finally, operational resilience has anchored us amid 11% quarter-over-quarter jumps in cocoa and palm oil costs. Hedging and supplier diversity capped COGS inflation at 4.2%, versus the sector's 6.8% per Circana. A new automated line in Reno lifted throughput 25% and trimmed labor 8%, dropping inventory days to 52 from 68, with 98.2% service levels. In LATAM, local-currency growth hit 11% despite Brazilian FX woes, via agile pricing and local innovations like mango NovaSnax for the $1.8 billion tropical snack market.

These efforts powered 6.2% organic growth, 420 basis points ahead of CPG peers, with adjusted EBITDA margins up 110 basis points to 19.8%. We're lifting FY24 guidance to 5-6% organic sales growth and 19.5-20% margins. We'll keep pruning for 12-15% ROIC, expanding digital against mass/club softness, and leading on ESG for enduring advantages. With that, I'll turn it over to Sarah for financial details.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Jordan. As Jordan outlined, we had a strong quarter. Net sales reached $3.2 billion, up 5.8% year-over-year. Organic net sales growth was 6.2% on an FX-neutral basis. Gross margin expanded to 46.2%, driven by favorable pricing realization, productivity gains, and a richer product mix. Operating income came in at $485 million, reflecting 12% growth. Diluted earnings per share were $1.52. We maintained tight cost control while funding growth investments.

Let me unpack the decomposition of our organic sales growth—volume, price, and mix—which highlights the balanced strength in our lineup. Organic growth totaled 6.2%, comprising volume up 2.1%, and price/mix up 4.1%. This mix shows effective pricing to counter past input inflation—now easing after 12-15% peaks on palm oil, PET, and corn—while spurring demand via new products and volume drivers.

Volume advanced 2.1% broadly, indicating solid consumer connection despite sluggish staples. In Home & Personal Care, our biggest segment at 45% of sales, volume climbed 2.8%, powered by PowerClean laundry—gaining 4.2 share points in North America per IRI—thanks to EcoShield concentrated pods, 50% denser with 30% less packaging, resonating with eco-minded younger households. Repeat rates rose 15% via the Clean for Good program linked to Walmart+ and Instacart.

Beauty & Grooming, 25% of sales, saw 1.9% volume lift, led by FreshGlow shampoos and RazorEdge men's grooming, with e-com now 22% of segment sales versus 18% prior. Our apex.com AI personalization, using AR for hair/scalp analysis, boosted conversions 28%.

Food & Beverage, 20% of sales, grew volume 1.2%, offset by premium FrostPeak ice cream's plant-based options up 12% on almond/oat formulas meeting EU clean-label standards, despite snack private label pressures.

By region, North America drove 2.5% volume via Costco SKU adds; Europe was +0.1% lapping COVID; Emerging Markets excelled at +5.4%, with Brazil PowerClean up 6 share through 15,000 rural depots, and India FreshGlow surging 20% in urban mid-tier.

Price/mix contributed 4.1%, led by +3.8% price from 4-6% list hikes on core items early quarter, steady on innovations. Mix added +0.3% from premiumization: Power Premium lines like EcoShield Ultra and FrostPeak Indulge now 28% of Home & Personal Care, up 400 bps, aiding 150 bps mix gain. Promo intensity fell to 22% of GRP from 26%, safeguarding equity.

North America price/mix +3.5%, Europe +4.2% on easing energy costs, Emerging +1.8% blending affordability and premiums like FrostPeak mochi in China at 8% frozen novelty share per NIQ.

This aligns with our Growth Accelerator: innovation (22 launches, 70% premium, 1.8 points growth); supply resilience (inventory to 65 days, OOS <5%); data distribution (Symphony AI for 4,000 SKUs, +2% facings); ESG products +15% volume in $1.4T market.

For Q4, expect 4-6% organic, volume 2.5-3% on seasons/launches like recyclable RazorEdge; price/mix 1.5-2.5% as inflation cools.

Next, our pricing actions and their sales impact were pivotal, fueling over half of organic growth amid 2.5% North America CPI—down from 9% peaks—and private label push from Walmart Great Value or Aldi. Net pricing realization, post trade spend and allowances, hit +4.2%, exceeding 3-4% guidance via list hikes, trade efficiency, and premium mix. Volume dipped -0.3% from elasticity in snacks/cleaners, but premiums offset; total sales $3.2B, +5.8%.

In North American Foods & Beverages (45% portfolio, NovaChips snacks, PureSpring RTD), +5.5% list hikes on 70% SKUs yielded +6.1% net pricing, +8.2% organic sales. AUR to $2.45 (+4.8%), volume -1.2% to value packs/Frito-Lay promos, but trade spend improved to 18.2% from 20.1% via AI platform with NielsenIQ, cutting over-promo 15%, holding 14.2% savory share (IRI), NPM +5.7%.

Personal Care/Household (35%), +3.8% net pricing: 4% hikes on EcoShield premiums, flat economy; +6.4% organic sales, stable volume, premium mix to 22% (+300 bps). Elasticity -0.6, like Colgate peers, vs. 28% private label in detergents.

EMEA (20%): +2.9% pricing under EU caps, EDLP on FreshGlow shampoos, +5.1% sales despite -1.5% volume from cost-of-living.

LATAM +12% organic, +8.4% pricing on NovaQuench vs. 15% inflation, +2% distribution to 85% ACV.

APAC +3.2%, 6% hikes on beauty, +9% sales on K-beauty.

Via Value Discipline: Precision Pricing Analytics (Kantar/Circana ML, -22% errors); Portfolio Optimization (divest 5 SKUs/2% sales, 12 innovations); Consumer Guardrails (7% annual cap/household).

Q4 pricing 2.5-3.5% as resins -10% QoQ, targeting 4-6% FY24 organic vs. industry +2.8%.

I'll now turn the call over to Mike to discuss marketing, promotions, and brand performance.

Mike Larson:
Thank you, Sarah. We saw robust results across our brands this quarter. Let me start with performance by key categories and brands, where we outpaced the CPG average of 3.8% per NielsenIQ with 6.2% organic growth on constant currency, blending 2.1% volume and 4.0% pricing against 5.2% input inflation (down from Q2's 7.1% on cocoa/sugar/PET).

Beverages led at +8.4% organic, +110 bps share to 14.2% (IRI), on 3.5% volume/+4.9% pricing. AquaFizz sparkling (natural flavors) +12.7%, household ACV to 28.4% (+2.3 pts), new zero-sugar electrolytes $45M incremental vs. LaCroix. HydroBoost (Gatorade-like) +9.2%, e-com +28% Amazon/DTC. NA 65% growth; LATAM +6.8% sachets; Europe rPET 45% bottles +8 Kantar favorability. BevTech 2.0: $120M for fermentation, 15% cost cut, 20 low-sugar SKUs.

Snacks/Confectionery +5.1%, +5.2% pricing/flat volume vs. +45% cocoa to $10k/ton (Hershey/Mondelez). +60 bps share to 11.8% (Circana). CrunchBar protein +11.3%, premiums 35%, +4.2 ppts margin via Vietnam blockchain nuts, 92% club ACV. ZestChips veggie +7.8%, SnackSmart app +18% repeats US; UK -1.2% vs. Tesco privates. APAC +9.5% puffy singles; pruning chocolate for $80M R&D jackfruit.

Beauty/Personal Care +4.7%, +1.8% volume/+2.9% pricing, +80 bps to 9.6% (Euromonitor), margins +120 bps to 52.3%. GlowEssence clean skincare +13.4% hyaluronic/SPF, DTC 22% (+7 pts) TikTok 3.5M UGC, Gen Z 45% new. SilkWave hair +6.2%, colorants +2.1% at-home kits. Europe +7.2% bio-pack 60%; China +5% Tmall; MENA SilkWave +12% halal. BeautyForge digital twin -30% time-to-market, 5 Q4 launches.

Household Essentials +3.9%, +0.9% volume/+3.0% pricing, share 13.1%. PureShield cleaners +8.1% disinfection/plant-based +3 pts natural; FreshWash +4.5% enzyme cold-water. NA flat volume +1.2 pts Walmart; EM India +7.4% sachets/Brazil +6.1%. HomeOptix ERP 92% forecast, -18% inventory ($250M), $400M wipes acquire for 7% CAGR $15B.

Overall: 55% innovation, +1.4 pts ACV, pricing; ESG Scope 3 -12% regen ag 50k farmers +9% loyalty (YouGov). NA 5.5%, Europe 6.8%, EM 8.2% (-1.1 ppt FX). Q4 5-7%, $300M savings to marketing/innovation.

Turning to our promotional strategy and effectiveness, which powered over 40% of volume amid trade spend norms of 20-25% (IRI/Nielsen). Promo ROI hit 3.2x (vs. 2.7x prior, 2.4x industry), via -15% non-performers (TPR <1.5x ROI or >5% base erosion). Trade % steady 22%, shifting 12 pts from EDLP to targeted.

TPRs 55% spend, 18% sales lift (Circana), AI elasticity with PROS on IRI data: 15-20% off NovaChips-like chips 2.5x ROI Walmart 92% ACV, suppress 10% low-traffic $45M save.

Feature/display 25% spend/35% volume: 18k end-caps +25% YoY Kroger/Albertsons +22% basket (1.2 extra SKUs), +110 bps household share to 14.2% vs. private laundry.

Digital/loyalty 20%, app coupons 42% redeem (vs. 20% norm), geo-fenced Target BOGO energy 28% conversion/4.1x ROI, $20M Adobe.

NA (65% budget) 3.5x ROI snacks +11% vs. -3% category; Europe (20%) 2.8x health bundles Tesco/Carrefour +7% share HFSS regs; EM (15%) 4.5x Brazil/India digital detergents +35% velocity; China 12% lift Alibaba countered by WeChat exclusives.

Future-proofing: cap TPR 12/SKU (vs. 18), 30% promos sustainability, Promo Optimizer Snowflake/Tableau $150M save 2yrs, 20% retailer-funded RFPs.

Q4 ROI 3.2-3.4x, 5-7% volume; risks privates 22% share/tariffs, but 70/30 sourcing. Drove 250 bps margin expansion.

Recent campaigns like our GlowEssence TikTok-driven push and CrunchBar club exclusives resonated, with new ZestChips veggie launch generating strong early buzz and trial.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for questions: press star then 1 on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs.

Emily Carter:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the details of the new marketing campaign and its impact on sales?

Mike Larson:
Good morning, Emily. Absolutely, happy to expand. Our latest campaigns, particularly around GlowEssence and the CrunchBar relaunch, have been highly effective in driving both awareness and sales lift. For GlowEssence, we leveraged TikTok Shop with user-generated content challenges that amassed over 3.5 million impressions, translating to a 13.4% organic sales surge in clean beauty. DTC penetration hit 22% of category revenue, with Gen Z accounting for 45% of new buyers—directly contributing about 2 points to overall beauty volume growth. On CrunchBar, our club channel focus with performance-based slotting secured 92% ACV in Costco/Sam's, boosting basket size 12% via multipacks and yielding 11.3% growth, or roughly 1.5 points to snacks organic. These tied into our broader promo playbook, like digital loyalty BOGOs, which saw 42% redemption rates and 4.1x ROI, powering 30% non-perishable lift. Overall, marketing drove 35% of incremental volume this quarter, aligning with our ROI target of 3.2x and supporting the 6.2% top-line.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with JPMorgan.

David Kim:
What are your plans for addressing rising commodity costs in the coming quarters?

Sarah Chen:
Hi David. Commodity pressures, like the 45% cocoa spike to $10,000 per ton or lingering PET/resin, are top of mind, but we've structured robust mitigation. Our hedging covers 70% of key exposures out six months, capping COGS inflation at 4.2% versus industry 6.8%. Supplier diversification—e.g., blockchain nuts Vietnam for CrunchBar, regen ag with Cargill—cut effective costs, plus portfolio shifts: divesting low-margin chocolate lines to fund cocoa alternatives like jackfruit. Operationally, Reno automation +25% throughput/-8% labor, HomeOptix ERP 92% accuracy/-18% inventory ($250M), keeping service 98%. Pricing discipline added +4.2% realization, with Q4 at 2.5-3.5% as inputs stabilize (-10% resins QoQ). Productivity $300M reinvested, targeting 19.5-20% EBITDA margins. In EM, local sourcing 70/30 mitigates tariffs. This playbook held gross margins at 46.2%, and we'll sustain outperformance.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Patel with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Patel:
How is the current inflationary environment impacting consumer demand for your premium product lines?

Jordan Hayes:
Thanks, Lisa. Inflation at 2.5% CPI has spurred some trade-down, with promo-sensitive households at 28% of U.S. volume per Kantar, but our premiums are resilient—growing 14% versus total 6.2%. Premium SKUs now 42% snacks, 28% home care, 35% CrunchBar, commanding 25% price premium via health/ESG halos like plant-based, rPET (95% packaging), Scope 3 -12%. Elasticity -0.6 in personal care shows loyalty akin to P&G/Unilever. Innovations like AquaFizz electrolytes ($45M), GlowEssence serums captured share from LaCroix/CeraVe amid low-cal/clean trends. Digital personalization 65% repeats DTC, omnichannel 22% NA sales. Consumer guardrails cap 7% annual hikes/household avoided backlash. In EM, aspirational premiums like NovaQuench LATAM +12%, FrostPeak China 8% share. Overall, premiums drove mix +1.5 points, with loyalty +9% YouGov, positioning for sustained demand.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Lee with Barclays.

Robert Lee:
Can you discuss the performance of your e-commerce channel this quarter?

Mike Larson:
Hi Robert. E-commerce was a standout, now 22% NA sales (from 14%), tracking to 25% FY25. DTC NovaCorp Direct +45% to $180M run-rate, 65% repeats via AI subs. HydroBoost Amazon/DTC +28%, GlowEssence TikTok 22% category DTC +3.5M UGC. Partnerships: Instacart Whole Foods +28% natural, Target Plus +15% Gen Z. APAC Shopee/Lazada HydroBoost +62%, +200 bps SEA share to 12.4% Kantar. Loyalty app geo-fence 28% conversion BOGO, 42% coupon redeem digital promos. VelocityMax AI planograms +15% C-store AquaFizz. Challenges like China pricing wars countered by Tmall/WeChat exclusives. Drove 30% non-perish lift, key to 2.1% volume amid staples softness.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Jordan Hayes for closing remarks.

Jordan Hayes:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your questions and participation in today's call. We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaCorp Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
